blocks.md: Africa is the second-largest continent and is crossed by the **Equator** near its middle. Much of it is a high **plateau**. The great **Rift Valley** runs from east Africa, with high mountains such as **Kilimanjaro** (the highest in Africa) and **Mount Kenya**, and long lakes. In the north-west are the **Atlas Mountains**; in the south-east the **Drakensberg**. The **Sahara** in the north is the largest hot desert; the **Kalahari** and the **Namib** are in the south-west.

blocks.title: Rivers and lakes
blocks.md:
- **Nile**: flows north to the Mediterranean; one of the longest rivers in the world.
- **Congo**: flows through the Congo Basin to the Atlantic across the Equator twice.
- **Niger**: starts in the west highlands and bends through the Sahel to the Gulf of Guinea.
- **Zambezi**: flows to the Indian Ocean with the Victoria Falls.
- **Lake Victoria** is the largest lake in Africa; **Lake Chad** borders Cameroon.

**Climate belts.** Because the Equator crosses the continent, the climates are arranged in belts to its north and south: equatorial in the middle (Congo Basin, southern Cameroon), tropical wet-dry (savanna) on both sides, hot desert further out (the Sahara in the north, the Kalahari in the south), and Mediterranean climates in the far north and south-west tip. High land such as the Ethiopian Highlands and East African mountains is cooler.

blocks.title: Resources
blocks.md: Africa is rich in **minerals** and **energy**: **crude oil and gas** (Nigeria, Angola, Gabon, Cameroon and others), **gold** and **diamonds** (South Africa, Ghana, Botswana), **copper** (the Copperbelt of Zambia and DR Congo), **iron ore**, **bauxite** and **phosphates**. It also has **fertile farmland**, **forests**, **rivers for hydroelectric power** and great tourist attractions.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- The Sahara is a desert in northern Africa, not in Cameroon.
- The Nile flows north, towards the Mediterranean Sea.
- Resources do not guarantee wealth: minerals must be processed, transported and fairly managed.

blocks.title: Example 1: a river and its sea
blocks.statement: Into which sea or ocean does the Nile flow, and in which general direction?
steps: The Nile begins in the highlands near the Equator.
It flows through Sudan and Egypt.
It flows north into the Mediterranean Sea.

blocks.title: Example 2: climate belts
blocks.statement: Why does Africa have similar climates north and south of the Equator?
steps: The Equator crosses the middle of the continent.
So belts repeat on both sides of the Equator.
blocks.answer: Because climate depends on distance from the Equator, which lies in the middle of Africa.
